newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon reports lower earnings for 1996.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon reports lower earnings for 1996.

text.p: Raytheon Co., which last week won a multibillion-dollar bidding war for Hughes Electronics' defence unit, Monday reported lower fourth-quarter profits of $177.4 million.

Raytheon said the $9.5 billion stock-and-debt purchase of Hughes Aircraft from General Motors Corp. and the $2.95 billion cash purchase earlier this month of Texas Instruments Inc.'s defence electronics unit would slightly hurt 1997 earnings -- but would provide a minimal boost in 1998 and increasingly help profits in subsequent years.
Raytheon's earnings, equal to 75 cents a share, compared with profits of $222.3 million, or 92 cents a share, in 1995's fourth quarter but met Wall Street analysts' expectations.
Raytheon stock dropped 50 cents to $48.125 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
For the quarter, Raytheon had $3.367 billion in sales vs. $3.360 billion in the year-ago quarter.
Lexington, Mass.-based Raytheon makes the Patriot air defence missile system, commercial and defence electronics, aircraft and major appliances. It also has an engineering and construction unit.

For the year, the company had profits of $761.2 million, or $3.21 a share, on sales of $12.26 billion, the highest in the company's history. In 1995, Raytheon earned $792.5 million, or $3.25 a share, on $11.716 billion in sales.
Raytheon on Thursday defeated Northrop Grumman Corp. in the bidding war for Hughes Aircraft, one of the last big prizes in the rapidly consolidating defence industry.

"Raytheon's 75th anniversary year is off to a fitting and historic start," company Chairman Dennis Picard said in a statement. "In this new year, our company has taken decisive steps to join with new defence electronics teammates to meet the competitive challenges and market opportunities of the future.

"We will become an even more competitive top-tier player in a consolidating defence industry, and we will remain a major participant in both established and emerging commercial markets around the world," he said.
